price.note: The Ramp tab's live default (fields.LPCS.fuel_per_litre), fixed at build time — the strip has no per-field pricing because the wear model has no concept of which aerodrome you're at ('No NK_ variable exists: Aerodrome fees, landings by field'). A price change means a new build and a sim restart, same as every other strip price.

strip_accumulation_rule.accumulation: On every CONFIRMED read (see reload_safety below), in this exact order: (1) compute delta = current L:NK_ST_FP5L_USED − L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L; (2) if delta > 0, add delta to L:NK_LG_FUEL_L_TOTAL — if delta <= 0, add nothing (a drop means FP5L.js reset the counter at a refuel, and must never post a negative cost); (3) THEN, regardless of the sign of delta, set L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L = current L:NK_ST_FP5L_USED. Step 3 is mandatory even when step 2 added nothing: if the baseline were left at its pre-refuel value, the next read's delta would be computed against a stale, too-high baseline and would go negative too, silently swallowing every litre burned after the refuel. Baseline tracks 'last confirmed reading', full stop — it is not conditioned on whether that reading contributed litres.

persisted_state.L:NK_LG_FUEL_L_TOTAL: Running total litres accumulated this way. Persisted. Multiplied by strip_accumulation_rule.price.eur_per_litre at display time to fold into the strip's running euro total — litres are stored, not euros, so a future price rebuild does not require re-deriving historical litres from an old blended euro figure.
persisted_state.L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L: The L:NK_ST_FP5L_USED value as of the last CONFIRMED read, updated every confirmed read per step 3 above regardless of delta sign. Advances in lockstep with L:NK_LG_BASELINE_MXLOG / L:NK_LG_BASELINE_TACH in STRIP_SPEC.md — never updated independently of the main cursor, and never skipped just because a given read didn't add litres.

strip_accumulation_rule.reload_safety: Gated by the same (NK_ST_MX_LOG, NK_ST_TACH) cursor as every other posting. On a reload/crash read (posting_cursor.rule_reload_or_crash), do not update L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L and do not touch L:NK_LG_FUEL_L_TOTAL — exactly as no other posting happens on a reload. This is why the baseline is a separate persisted variable rather than re-reading FP5L_USED cold each time: it lets a reload leave the fuel accumulator exactly where it was, the same guarantee the maintenance/hours cursor already gives.
strip_accumulation_rule.laptop_book_unaffected: The laptop ledger keeps billing fuel exactly as in read_rule/fallback above — per-field priced, from the same FP5L_USED-before-uplift reading where available. This rule only concerns the strip's own separate running total.

fp5l_edge_cases.status: K7b section 5. Verified by Records line by line against FP5L.js (live ed8f5deb).
fp5l_edge_cases.unpowered: FP5L.js returns early while isElectricityAvailable() is false, and does not advance lastFuel. When power returns the whole unpowered burn arrives as one step, and counts only if it is under 2 L. Anything bigger is dropped.
fp5l_edge_cases.large_single_drops: Any single-update drop of 2 L or more is ignored outright (line 107 tests 0 < dF < 2). assumption, from the V261 recorder finding: an html gauge paused off screen produces exactly such jumps.
fp5l_edge_cases.burn_lost_at_a_refuel: The strip reads USED only at confirmed cursor reads, so litres burnt between the last confirmed read and a refuel are lost when the refuel resets USED. Accepted for now. The strip kit may read every update instead.
fp5l_edge_cases.consequence_for_the_contract: burnL inherits all three gaps whatever its burn_source. The record says which source it used and the book labels anything but the logger, so a figure that went through these gaps is never presented as exact.

burn_source_chain.status: K7c C2. Written out here because revision 3 carried it only in LEG_CONTRACT.md and the vectors.
burn_source_chain.logger: burnL summed from the laptop logger rows: the sum of the fp5l_used increases between the lb_open 0 -> 1 transition and the lb_n increment. The only rung that survives a refuel inside the leg, because it adds increases instead of subtracting endpoints.
burn_source_chain.aircraft: V274 saves L_FUEL_DEP and L_FUEL_ARR as FP-5L USED readings, so the leg burn is L_FUEL_ARR - L_FUEL_DEP. THERE IS NO STORED burnL VARIABLE. **Allowed only when refuelInLeg is false** - a refuel resets USED, so the subtraction comes out negative or tiny and V274 itself reports "no leg burn". Same guard as rem. This is C2: revision 3 let this rung fire across a refuel.
burn_source_chain.rem: fp5lStart - fp5lShutdown, the REM tank totals. Allowed only when refuelInLeg is false, for the same reason in reverse: a refuel raises the tank mid-leg and the subtraction loses everything burnt before it.
burn_source_chain.uplift: The typed uplift. Last resort, always labelled.
burn_source_chain.none: A refuel with no logger, no usable aircraft figure and no uplift: nothing is billed and the review page says exactly that. Guessing from the endpoints would be worse than billing nothing.
burn_source_chain.inherited_gaps: Every rung that reads USED inherits the FP-5L gaps in fp5l_edge_cases: a single-update drop of 2 L or more is never counted, and nothing counts while the instrument is unpowered.

rule_scaled_continuous.billing_normalisation: To price a service/repair, divide the OBSERVED condition loss by the R that was in force when it happened, so a part serviced after 6 minutes of sim time at x1000 is billed as 6 minutes' worth of REAL wear, not 6 minutes × 1000.

rule_scaled_by_r_only.billing_normalisation: Same principle: divide observed loss by R before pricing.

rule_starter_capped.spec_ref: SPEC §2.2 ('the rate factor is capped at 100')
rule_starter_capped.billing_normalisation: Divide by min(R, 100), not R — the wear model treats x100 and x1000 identically for the starter, so the same starter cost applies at either setting.

rule_never_scaled.note: No adjustment needed at any Wear rate setting; scheduled checks and hourly reserves already price off real elapsed hours.

rule_r_zero.rule: No loss accrues at all. Bill nothing for wear at this setting. Never divide by 0 — R=0 short-circuits before any normalisation formula runs.

rule_r_changes_mid_leg.fact: A Wear/Failure rate change works at any time and bumps NK_ST_MX_LOG.
rule_r_changes_mid_leg.rule: Normalise each loss with the R that was in force when it happened. With end-of-leg reads only (the ledger's current model), a leg whose MX_LOG step contains a rate-change action cannot be attributed with confidence — flag it 'rate changed mid-leg' for a manual check. No silent guess.
rule_r_changes_mid_leg.cold_start_cylinder_hit: The one-time cold-start cylinder hit (minus 0.05 × R once, SPEC §2.2) is subject to the same normalise-by-R treatment as the continuous losses, not exempt from it.
rule_r_changes_mid_leg.widened_by_the_pro_rata_decision: Under pro rata the flag has to cover more than one posting step. With design 1 (accumulator) it stays as written, because each read is normalised as it happens. With design 2 (snapshot) it must fire whenever R changed at any point since the part was last serviced, not just inside the step that posted.

DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.status: DECIDED — pro rata. Claus, F-BVNK Annunciator board item, 16 Sep 2026 14:47:46 local, relayed word for word by the PM: "Pro rata - bill only the wear that would have happened at REAL". Revision 2 of this kit is collapsed to that single reading; the full-catalogue-price reading is gone.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.rule: net_line = half-up(price_net × normalised_points / 100); vat = half-up(net_line × vat_pct / 100); gross = net_line + vat.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.normalised_points: The points of the part's life the service restores, expressed in REAL-equivalent condition points. Condition runs 0-100, so normalised_points / 100 is the fraction of the part's life actually consumed at REAL rate.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.divisor: R for rule_scaled_continuous and rule_scaled_by_r_only, min(R,100) for rule_starter_capped, 1 for rule_never_scaled. R = 0 posts nothing at all (rule_r_zero) and never reaches a divide.
worked_examples: V1 magneto, R=1, from condition 42: 58 points. net half-up(720.00 × 58/100) = 417.60; VAT half-up(417.60 × 23/100) = 96.05; gross 513.65.
V15 cylinder, R=1000, from condition 35: 0.065 points. net half-up(2250.00 × 0.065/100) = 1.46; VAT 0.34; gross 1.80.
V16 brakes, R=100, from condition 70: 0.3 points. net half-up(1089.43 × 0.3/100) = 3.27; VAT 0.75; gross 4.02.
V25 brakes, 1 point: net 10.89; VAT 2.50; gross 13.39. Gross-first would give 13.40.
V26 brakes, 15 points: net 163.41; VAT 37.58; gross 200.99. Gross-first would give 201.00.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.what_this_does_not_touch: Hourly reserves, scheduled 25/50/100 h checks, fuel, aerodrome fees, hangar, insurance and CAO. Every one of those prices off real elapsed hours, litres or the calendar, never off a condition loss, so no divisor reaches them. Also untouched: the laptop ledger FBVNK-LEDGER.html, whose own health model runs on real flown hours with no R in it at all. If that book is ever fed the sim's NK_ST_C_* values, this rule starts applying to it too.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.overhaul_is_not_pro_rata: An overhaul (V14) is a whole-unit replacement at its catalogue figure, not a fraction of remaining life. 35,000.00 posts in full whatever the condition was. Same for a battery replacement and a propeller overhaul.
DECIDED_how_a_normalised_loss_becomes_eu.C3_order: K7c C3, the leader's decision. Net first, which is the order every other invoice line in this file already uses (see rounding.order_within_a_posting) - so a pro-rata service is not a special case any more. Revision 3 said price_gross × fraction, which rounds the VAT inside the gross before the fraction is applied and can land a cent high: brakes at 1 point is 13.39 net-first and 13.40 gross-first. None of the three existing vectors moves - V1 513.65, V15 1.80, V16 4.02 are the same under both orders - which is exactly why it went unnoticed until Records priced a 1-point and a 15-point service.

capture_requirement.why: A pro-rata posting needs to know how much life the service restored. A service is detected by the condition reading 100, which is after the fact — by then the pre-service value is gone. Nothing in revision 1 captured it, so pro rata was not computable from what the kit recorded. Named here, per the PM's request, so design note B25 (automatic leg capture) can carry it.

reads_needed_either_way.plus: NK_ST_OIL_QT (quarts, rule_scaled_by_r_only) — same treatment as the ten above.
reads_needed_either_way.plus_R: NK_ST_WEAR, LocalVar 58, already read. The divisor comes from it.
reads_needed_either_way.note: All eleven are existing package variables. No new SimVar, no new reader. What is new is persisting them between reads.

design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.how: On every confirmed (non-reload) read, for each part: drop = previous_condition − current_condition. If drop > 0, add drop / divisor_in_force_now to that part's accumulator. On a service (condition reads 100), bill price_gross × accumulator / 100 and zero the accumulator.
design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.why_this_one: It is exact when R changed during the part's life, because each read is normalised by the R that was actually in force for that read. The snapshot design below is only exact if R never moved since the last service — and a rate change between services is the normal case, not an edge one: R is a slider Claus moves.
design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.count: 22 new persisted LocalVars. Each needs a systems.cfg [LocalVars] entry — package bytes, so a Builder kit and the PM's install, not this session's work.
design_1_accumulator_RECOMMENDED.units: Accumulators hold REAL-equivalent condition points, floating point. Store × 1000 as integers if float drift is a concern; that is a Builder call, the arithmetic is the same.

design_2_snapshot_CHEAPER.how: Persist only the previous read's condition values. On a service, bill price_gross × ((100 − previous_condition) / divisor) / 100.
design_2_snapshot_CHEAPER.new_persisted_variables: The eleven L:NK_LG_PREV_* above, and nothing else. 11 instead of 22.
design_2_snapshot_CHEAPER.the_cost: Exact only when R was constant from the part's last service to this one. If R moved, the whole depletion is divided by whichever R happens to be in force at the moment of service, which is wrong in both directions: service at x1 after wearing the part at x1000 and the posting is 1000× too high. rule_r_changes_mid_leg must then widen from "R changed inside this posting step" to "R changed at any point since this part was last serviced", and flag rather than price.

capture_requirement.for_the_laptop_book: FBVNK-LEDGER.html takes its legs from the aeroplane as records (contract FBVNK_LEG/2, written out in LEG_CONTRACT.md in this folder). If a record is to carry a service, it carries conditionBefore and conditionAfter as maps keyed by the eleven variable names above, plus the R in force. No persistence problem on that side: the aeroplane holds the snapshot and sends it.

design_3_at_the_action.source: K7b section 4, verified against HANGAR.js act() line 189 (live 29919c4a).
design_3_at_the_action.how: The SERVICE action already calls this.L() in the same function. Immediately before this.set(item.key, 100), this.L(item.key) holds the exact pre-service condition and this.L("NK_ST_WEAR") holds the R at that instant. Write both to new L:NK_LG_* vars there. The same holds for the oil action (line 190) and for the seven parts in the overhaul action (line 191).
design_3_at_the_action.what_it_buys: The value AT the service, not at the last confirmed read. Both polling designs miss whatever wore between that read and the service.
design_3_at_the_action.what_it_does_not_buy: A part whose life spanned more than one R still needs per-read accumulation to divide correctly. This route replaces the snapshot, not the accumulator.
design_3_at_the_action.boundary_holds: It writes L:NK_LG_* only and no NK_ST_*, so the "reads the wear model, never writes it" rule is intact.
design_3_at_the_action.gate: canService() at line 188: on the ground, engine off, master on. It runs once per accepted action, and MX_LOG is bumped at line 199 immediately after.

oil_is_quarts_not_points.status: K7b also-fix, and the SPEC section 2.3 units.
oil_is_quarts_not_points.fact: NK_ST_OIL_QT is US quarts, 0 to 8, in an 8 qt sump. It is not a 0-100 condition value, so normalised_points / 100 does not apply to it as the service rule is written.
oil_is_quarts_not_points.consumption: Engine running: minus (0.05 + max(0, 75 - C_CYL)/50 x 0.9) qt/h x R. So 0.05 qt/h at C_CYL >= 75 and up to 1.4 qt/h at C_CYL 0. Scaled by R like the other by-R group.
oil_is_quarts_not_points.rule_when_a_price_exists: quarts_restored = 8 - OIL_QT_before. normalised_quarts = quarts_restored / R. posting = price_per_quart x normalised_quarts. Divide by quarts, never by 100 - the sump is 8 qt, not 100 points, and dividing a quart figure by 100 would under-bill by 8 to 1 on a full top-up.
oil_is_quarts_not_points.today: DORMANT. There is no oil price on file (prices_not_yet_defined), so a top-up posts nothing and raises the flag, per the PM. The rule is written now so that adding a price is a one-line change and not a fresh derivation.

posting_cursor.why_these_two: NK_ST_ENG_HRS is not safe alone — Overhaul sets it to 0 and Reset to delivery sets it to 300 (SPEC §2.1), so it goes backward on purpose. NK_ST_MX_LOG only increments, on every accepted page action, and Reset to delivery does not reset it (SPEC §2.4: '+1 (not reset)'). NK_ST_TACH is never touched by Reset to delivery.
posting_cursor.rule_reload_or_crash: Either number lower than the stored pair (not only TACH with MX_LOG unchanged — a crash can drop both at once) means the sim reloaded a save from before a crash or killed process (assumption, SPEC §1's own hedge: LocalVars save only on a normal exit). Post nothing. Never reverse an invoice already posted. The book stops advancing until BOTH numbers pass the last confirmed point again — no double billing, no silent refund.
posting_cursor.rule_mx_log_higher: MX_LOG higher than stored, on its own, posts the maintenance action(s) it represents.
posting_cursor.rule_tach_higher: TACH higher than stored, on its own, accrues the hourly items (engine/propeller reserves; scheduled-check hour counting).
posting_cursor.rule_independent: Either or both of the above can be true on a given read — this is not an AND condition.

rule_multi_step_jump.fact: A jump of more than 1 in MX_LOG between two reads means more than one action happened at once.

rule_overhaul_consumes_the_step.status: K7b F3. Verified by Records against HANGAR.js line 191, the ovh action.
rule_overhaul_consumes_the_step.fact: One Overhaul action, and so one MX_LOG step, sets NK_ST_C_CYL, MAG, CARB, OIL, ALT, STR and VAC to 100, ENG_HRS to 0 and OIL_QT to 8, all together.
rule_overhaul_consumes_the_step.the_bug_it_prevents: Read through the plain detection table, that one action matches seven services, a top-up and the overhaul. At R=1 from Reset-to-delivery levels (85) the four priced parts alone would add 815.50 on top of the 35,000.00 engoh: cyl 2,767.50 + mag 885.60 + alt 1,094.70 + vac 688.80, each x 0.15. K7b quotes 815.49, which is the same money summed first and rounded once at the end; the rounding rule decided in F2 rounds once per posting line, and each of the four is its own line, so the book would have shown 815.50. Two of the four are .xx5 cases in their own right, 415.125 and 164.205.
rule_overhaul_consumes_the_step.rule: An MX_LOG step whose read shows NK_ST_ENG_HRS at 0 posts engoh and nothing else. The seven engine parts reading 100 in that same step post nothing, and OIL_QT reading 8 in that same step posts nothing. The overhaul consumes them: they are what an overhaul IS, not nine separate jobs.
rule_overhaul_consumes_the_step.discriminator_unchanged: Reset to delivery also seeds those parts, but to 85 and not 100, and sets ENG_HRS to 300. ENG_HRS 0 means overhaul; ENG_HRS 300 with the full seed set means Reset. See V3 and V14.
rule_overhaul_consumes_the_step.vector: V14, extended in this revision with the seven conditions before and after.

reset_to_delivery.billing_impact: None. Logged as one tech-log entry (timestamp, MX_LOG value, 'Reset to delivery — test action, not billed'). Never an invoice line, never touches the euro total, cost per hour, or the engine/propeller reserve funds — Reset to delivery is a wear-model convenience, not a real overhaul.
reset_to_delivery.new_battery_action: A new battery is the separate 3-click ammeter-pad action (SPEC §2.5) and is not part of Reset to delivery.

rounding.status: DECIDED — the PM, 16 Sep 2026, on K7b F2.
rounding.rule: Round half-up on the exact decimal value, to the cent, once per posting line.
rounding.never: Never toFixed. Never Math.round on a float. Both read the binary double, not the decimal value, and 31.185 is stored just below .185: (31.185).toFixed(2) gives 31.18 where this rule gives 31.19.
rounding.how: Integer cents where the inputs are already cents - net_cents x (100 + vat) / 100, half-up - or a decimal routine. A float is acceptable only if the rounding itself is done on decimal digits: snap the binary noise off with toPrecision(15), then read the third decimal and carry.
rounding.order_within_a_posting: net to the cent first; VAT computed off the ROUNDED net and rounded; gross is the sum of the two. That way the invoice adds up to its own printed lines.
rounding.both_readers: The laptop ledger and the future HANGAR strip must use the same routine. The laptop book FBVNK-LEDGER.html implements it as eur2(); 23 test cases pass, including the two .xx5 cases.
rounding.what_it_changes: V6 becomes 31.19 (31.185 exact), and V6 stays the vector that pins a .xx5 case. V18 is added as a second one, on a real invoice.
rounding.pro_rata_order: K7c C3. A pro-rata service rounds in the same order as everything else: the normalised fraction is applied to the NET, that net is rounded to the cent, VAT is computed off the rounded net and rounded, and gross is the sum. Never price_gross × fraction - that rounds VAT into the gross before the fraction and can land a cent high. The book and the strip must both do it this way.

hours_sources.reserves_accrue_on: NK_ST_TACH - THE HOUR METER, IN BOTH HALVES. DECIDED by Claus on the Annunciator, 16 Sep 2026 at 21:05:42 local, word for word: "Tacho time (the hour meter)". The cockpit strip was already on it and is unchanged; the laptop book moved to it in R6, having been accruing on airborne time. Airborne time now keeps the carnet's Heures de Vol and the airborne totals, and nothing else. It is the meter's PROGRESSION between records that accrues, not a leg's own tachStop - tachStart: under V275 only airborne legs become records, so the taxi, run-up and ground running between them sits in the gap and a real hour meter counts it. See accrual_clock.
hours_sources.note_on_sim_rate: CORRECTED in R4, K7c also-fix. Revision 3 said every hours variable undercounts at sim rates above 1x, and claimed the reserves under-bill because of it. That is wrong for TACH. TACH (interior XML line 215) adds unclamped A:GENERAL ENG ELAPSED TIME deltas; only ENG_HRS and AF_HRS (line 1365) add the tick that is clamped to 1 s. The reserves accrue on TACH, so they do NOT under-bill from the clamp. assumption, and labelled as one: that A:GENERAL ENG ELAPSED TIME itself follows the sim rate. ENG_HRS and AF_HRS do undercount at rate, which matters for the engine-life figure and for airborne time, not for money.

carnet_entry_rule.claus_16_sep_1834: I want to remark. If NO airborne event, no log entry at all. Eg, engine starts, taxi etc. if no airborne (flight even) NO log book entry. Only airborne (flight time) events goes into the logbook. So, from time to time there may be a tacho log entry "discrepency" between last leg and current (last) leg - just like real world, so just accept this.
carnet_entry_rule.rule: The test is the AIRBORNE EVENT and it is not the noTakeOff flag. An air start is spawned airborne: noTakeOff true, airborne time real, and it IS a carnet entry. When the record carries an airborne figure that figure decides; when it carries none the book falls back to whether a take-off or landing time exists.
carnet_entry_rule.still_posts: A run that is not a flight is still filed and still posts - it burnt fuel and it ran the engine. It is kept off the carnet page, the Logbook tab says how many, and the Ledger has them in full.
carnet_entry_rule.tacho_gap: Not an error. No tacho continuity check exists in the book and none ever did. The Logbook page states the gap a left-out run leaves is expected.
carnet_entry_rule.fuel_between_legs: Billed by nothing today. The gap is measurable off the FP-5L - previous leg's fp5lArr less this leg's fp5lStart - so it needs no assumed burn rate. PROPOSED, NOT BUILT: bill that difference when it is positive and no uplift is declared between the two, at the departure field's price, labelled on the review page. At Cascais's 2.30 EUR/L a 3 L gap is 6.90 EUR gross and a 10 L gap 23.00 EUR. This session has no measured ground burn rate for F-BVNK and assumes none: the one real ground run carries a refuel, fp5l 231 -> 234, so no burn is readable from it.
carnet_entry_rule.v275: The aircraft side will stop closing a leg at all when the engine run never got airborne (PM, 18:36). Until it is installed the aeroplane can still produce such records, so the book keeps excluding them.

rule.normal: accrued hours = this record's tachStop less the previous record's tachStop, to 0.01 h
rule.first_record: its own tachStop - tachStart; the cursor is picked up there
rule.meter_backwards: a tachStart below the cursor is a reload or another machine. Flag it, post nothing negative, accrue this leg's own span, resume the cursor from the new reading. TACH never goes backwards in normal running: no reset touches it and it is seeded to 1246.58 only on a first install.
rule.no_reading: accrue the leg's airborne time rather than lose the hours, say so, and CARRY that figure: the next record with a real reading subtracts it from the measured gap so nothing is billed twice
rule.strip: reads NK_ST_TACH directly (LocalVar 11) under the (MX_LOG, TACH) cursor it already has. No change.
rule.bounded_after_K7e: K7e failed the revision 6 rule. A forward gap more than 5 h beyond the leg's own span, or an own span more than 5 h beyond the leg's own flying, is not one meter: accrue the leg's own time, flag it, resume. A record older than the last one filed never moves the cursor. A negative gap never moves the cursor. V37.
